module purpose: neorv32_gpio decodes bus requests into writes of per-pin registers (output value port_out, trigger type irq_typ, trigger polarity irq_pol, interrupt enable irq_en, pending-clear mask irq_clrn), drives port_out on gpio_o, samples gpio_i into port_in and port_in2, computes a per-pin trigger irq_trig from type and polarity, latches enabled triggers in irq_pend, drives cpu_irq_o as the OR of the pending bits, and returns registers and sampled inputs on bus_rsp_o.data on reads.

use-case flows.value: write eligibility of a bus request to one of the GPIO registers (strobe, write direction, register address)
output pin value taken from bus write data, held in port_out and driven on gpio_o
per-pin interrupt trigger type and polarity taken from bus write data and held in irq_typ and irq_pol
per-pin interrupt enable taken from bus write data, held in irq_en and applied to the pending update
input pin values sampled from gpio_i into port_in and, one clock later, into port_in2
per-pin trigger decision: level or edge of the sampled input selected by trigger type and polarity
pending interrupt bits latched from enabled triggers and the CPU interrupt request derived from them
pending bits cleared where a bus write to the pending register writes 0 into irq_clrn (all ones otherwise)
sampled inputs, output value, trigger type, trigger polarity, enable and pending bits returned on a read
all registers and the outputs cleared to zero while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Register write access -- whether a bus request is allowed to update one of the GPIO registers
conceptual assets.reasoning: Every configure flow and the pending-clear flow depend on the write predicate `if (bus_req_i.stb = '1')` (line 71), `if (bus_req_i.rw = '1')` (line 72) and `case bus_req_i.addr(4 downto 2)` (line 73), which select which register takes bus_req_i.data (lines 74-78). Integrity is Established: a register must change only when these conditions hold for its address. Mapping limitation: the decision is made inline in the process, with no declared signal holding it, and every operand is a field of bus_req_i, a record carrying complete read/write transactions (addr, data, ben, stb, rw; answered by bus_rsp_o ack, err, data, lines 66-68). Transport records are excluded whole and by field, so no eligible declaration remains and the list is empty.

conceptual assets.concept: Output pin value configuration -- the value the module drives on its GPIO output pins
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores bus write data with `when addr_out_c => port_out <= bus_req_i.data(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0);` (line 74) and drives it out with `gpio_o(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0) <= port_out;` (line 112). The consumer of gpio_o is not supplied, so integrity is Established from the delivering lines: gpio_o must carry exactly the last written value. Availability is also Established: the value is held between writes (port_out, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 74) and driven continuously by the combinational process (lines 109-112); it is read back at line 84. port_out stores it and its own CARRIES record into the output port gpio_o (occurrence 6, line 112) shows the use. gpio_o is the exit port (COPIES port_out, occurrence 3, line 112); bits above GPIO_NUM-1 are tied to zero by line 111. bus_req_i.data and bus_rsp_o.data are transport fields and are not listed. No line restricts reading port_out, so confidentiality is not established.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt trigger mode configuration -- per-pin choice of level or edge and of polarity
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores `irq_typ <= bus_req_i.data(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0);` (line 75) and `irq_pol <= bus_req_i.data(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0);` (line 76); the trigger computation reads both through `sel_v := irq_typ(i) & irq_pol(i);` (line 123) and `case sel_v is` (line 124), which chooses low level, high level, falling edge or rising edge for irq_trig (lines 125-128). Integrity is Established: a corrupted bit changes which input condition sets the pending bit at line 141. Availability: both settings are held between writes (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, lines 75-76) and read back (lines 85-86). The map has no SELECTS record from irq_typ or irq_pol to irq_trig because the selection passes through the process variable sel_v (lines 123-124); the RTL is the authority. Their recorded use is CARRIES into the output field bus_rsp_o.data (occurrence 4, lines 85-86). Type and polarity together form the one 2-bit selector, so they realize one concept.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt enable configuration -- per-pin setting that decides whether a trigger may become and stay pending
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores `irq_en <= bus_req_i.data(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0);` (line 77), and the pending update reads it as `irq_pend <= irq_en and ((irq_pend and irq_clrn) or irq_trig);` (line 141, SOURCES irq_pend at occurrence 5). Integrity is Established: a 0 bit forces the pending bit to 0 and a 1 bit lets a trigger set it, so a wrong enable suppresses or creates interrupt requests on cpu_irq_o (line 142). Availability: held between writes (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 77) and read back (line 87). irq_en stores the setting.

conceptual assets.concept: Sampled input pin value -- the GPIO input levels as captured by the module
conceptual assets.reasoning: The input flow captures `port_in <= gpio_i(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0);` (line 103) on each rising edge of clk_i while rstn_i is high, and the module uses the captured value to decide triggers (lines 125-128) and returns it on a read (line 83). Integrity is Established: the trigger decision and the read-back value must reflect the sampled pins. gpio_i sets the value (SOURCES port_in, occurrence 2, line 103), since this entity reads it to store it. port_in stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 103); its GATES records on irq_trig (occurrences 9-10, lines 127-128) show the use. port_in2 is not listed: `port_in2 <= port_in;` (line 104) makes it a register whose only COPIES record names port_in, so it holds port_in's value one clock later. No line restricts reading port_in, so confidentiality is not established.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-pin interrupt trigger decision -- whether a pin's input meets its configured trigger condition this cycle
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_trig is computed in the generate loop (lines 119-131): `when "10" => irq_trig(i) <= (not port_in(i)) and port_in2(i);` (line 127) and `when "11" => irq_trig(i) <= port_in(i) and (not port_in2(i));` (line 128), with level cases at lines 125-126, chosen by sel_v (lines 123-124). Integrity is Established: the decision feeds the pending update at line 141 (SOURCES irq_pend, occurrence 7), so a wrong decision sets a pending bit with no qualifying input or misses one. irq_trig computes the decision (GATED_BY port_in and port_in2, occurrence 5, line 128). port_in and port_in2 are operands of the decision, not the decision.

conceptual assets.concept: Pending interrupt state and CPU interrupt request -- latched per-pin interrupt events and the request raised from them
conceptual assets.reasoning: The report flow latches `irq_pend <= irq_en and ((irq_pend and irq_clrn) or irq_trig);` (line 141), a self-updating register (flow graph), and raises `cpu_irq_o <= or_reduce_f(irq_pend);` (line 142). The consumer of cpu_irq_o is not supplied, so integrity is Established from the delivering line: cpu_irq_o must be the OR of the pending bits, and each pending bit must follow line 141. Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: with rstn_i high, an enabled trigger is latched on the next rising edge and kept until cleared or disabled, and cpu_irq_o follows one edge later (lines 140-142). irq_pend stores the state (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 141; its SOURCES record into the output port cpu_irq_o at occurrence 6 shows the use; read back at line 88). cpu_irq_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM irq_pend, occurrence 3, line 142), ahead of its own registered storage.

conceptual assets.concept: Pending-interrupt clear command -- the per-pin mask a bus write uses to clear pending bits
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_clrn is set to all ones on every clock edge (`irq_clrn <= (others => '1');`, line 69) unless a write to addr_ip_c loads bus write data (line 78), so it holds a one-cycle clear command. The pending update reads it as `(irq_pend and irq_clrn)` (line 141, SOURCES irq_pend at occurrence 5): a 0 bit clears that pending bit unless a new trigger occurs in the same cycle. Integrity is Established: a wrong mask clears a pending interrupt that was not acknowledged, or keeps one that was cleared, changing cpu_irq_o (line 142). irq_clrn stores the command (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 78); its value is a decision this entity reads in a computation, not data passed on. Reset sets it to all zeros (line 63), while irq_pend is also reset (line 138).
